### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.pairs

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

Hello,

I have noticed something weird after I've started to use `mini.pairs`. When working with Svelte files, the `<CR>` inside JS and SCSS does not indent properly in curly brackets blocks. It shifts both the new line and the closing curly bracket one step too far. This behaviour does NOT happen in regular JS  or SCSS files. And it comes back to normal when I disable `mini.pairs`.

It is worth noting that my indentation is set to 2 spaces and I have `autoindent` on. And I use tree sitter's Svelte module. 

I have also tried to wait a long time between typing `{` and `<CR>` to ensure there is no mapping that involves both characters in combination. I didn't set such mapping myself, but I tried just in case. It does not change anything to the described behaviour.

When I inspect with `:imap <CR>`, the `mini.pairs` `cr()` function is what comes up.

Does anybody experience the same? Maybe in similar multi language files like Vue, Astro or React?

### Reproduction

So here is what I get when I type `<CR>` after the opening curly bracket. The pipe represents my cursor.

```html
<style lang='scss' >

  section {
      |
    }

</style>
```

That is inside a `.svelte` file with `autoindent` on, the tree sitter svelte module and indentation set to 2 spaces.

I can only reproduce when `vim.o.smartindent` is true.

I started with the following lines in "test.svelte":

```svelte

<style lang='scss'>

  section|

</style>

```

Now, when cursor is on the end of "section", the following keystrokes reproduce: `a {<CR>`.

Without 'mini.pairs', the result is as expected with keystrokes `a {<CR>}<Esc>O`:

```svelte

<style lang='scss'>

  section {
    |
  }

</style>

```
@abeldekat ah thanks for confirming ! Indeed I forgot to mention `smartindent` which I have on as well.

Just an observation:

With 'https://github.com/windwp/nvim-autopairs', the behavior is correct, both with and without `vim.o.smartindent`.
Using mini, the result differs when `vim.o.smartindent` is true.

The treesitter part is not relevant. The issue arises when `vim.o.smartindent = true`.

New init.lua:

```lua

-- https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yml
-- See section "reproduction"
vim.pack.add({ 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim' })

-- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior:

vim.o.autoindent = true -- Use auto indent
vim.o.shiftwidth = 2 -- Use this number of spaces for indentation
vim.o.smartindent = true -- Make indenting smart

require('mini.pairs').setup()

```

I found a related discussion: [Filetype dependent indent on <CR> within parentheses](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2042).

Quoting:
> ...
> There is nothing filetype dependent in 'mini.pairs' per se. But the <CR> implementation uses the approach that mimics the most robust approach that also respects filetype: pressing <CR> with 'mini.pairs' is basically the [same as pressing <CR><C-o>O](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/126ce3328c78399dcff58272f6f540a373b62a75/doc/mini-pairs.txt#L328-L330) without 'mini.pairs'. Here <C-o> temporarily exits into Normal mode and O inserts an empty line above (usually properly indented; at least with default value of 'indentkeys').
> ...

That typing sequence works as expected when using filetype 'scss' instead of 'svelte', given the same testfile content.


For svelte however, the result of `{}<Esc>i<CR>`, *without mini.pairs*,  is:

```svelte
<style lang="scss">

  section {
    }


</style>
```

@abeldekat my understanding is that if the cursor is between the curly brackets, then `<CR>`, then it should do something like `<CR><Esc>==O`.

The `==` is very significant here because when fiddling around without `mini.pairs` on, I have realised this is the major difference:

- in a regular CSS/SCSS file, after the return, the closing curly bracket is NOT indented
- in a svelte file, after the return line, the closing curly bracket IS indented

The regular CSS/SCSS smart indent is different, because it does something different depending on if you have nothing following your cursor, or if you have a closing curly bracket after your cursor. The rational is that the user will escape and the press "O" to add the inside.

Whereas the smart indent inside a svelte file always behaves the same way in both cases. It will ALWAYS add an indent. The rational being that the user will write the inside line by line and then on the last line will do `==` or `<<`.

None of them are entirely satisfying I guess, but this is the difference that breaks `mini.pairs` behaviour. I'd like to believe it would work with what I suggested, i.e. `<CR><Esc>==O`, but I might be wrong because I don't have all scenarios in mind.

But in the grand scheme of things, this is something that should be fixed at the core. Smart indent should behave the same everywhere. Not sure who this bug needs to be redirected to. The special svelte tree sitter module's maintainers? the core neovim maintainers? What do you reckon?

> ...
> Not sure who this bug needs to be redirected to
> ...

I am pretty sure it is not a [treesitter](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2591#issuecomment-6523882778) problem. Let's wait what @echasnovski has to say.

@abeldekat you're probably right. By curiosity I have just tried in an Astro file, which ressemble in the sense that you have nested file types. And in astro files, it works exactly like regular CSS/SCSS. The exact behaviour I described. So it suggests it is specific to `.svelte` files, which is why I thought about tree sitter because each file type has its own setup. But that is only a wild guess because I know next to nothing about tree sitter.

The problem might even be in vim. Given the same contents in testfile and keys `a {}<Esc>i<CR`:

- svelte

```svelte
<style lang="scss">

  section {
}

</style>
```

- scss

```scss
<style lang="scss">

  section {
  }

</style>
```

> Without 'mini.pairs', the result is as expected with keystrokes `a {<CR>}<Esc>O`:

The problem here is that this doesn't *quite* the same as what `<CR>` does: it needs to operate when both left and right parts are already present. As [per its logic](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-pairs.html#minipairs.cr). So the more accurate test is `{}<Left><CR><C-o>O` which *does* behave as with 'mini.pairs'.

The approach of `<CR><C-o>O` is the best compromise I could find here:
- Using `<CR><Esc>==O` is too much and it will indeed not universally work (`==` depends on 'equalprg', for example).
- Disabling 'smartindent' will not add extra indents, but it will also prevent from indenting the blank line.
- Implementing custom logic based on `nvim_buf_set_text()` or similar (which is probably what 'nvim-autopairs' does) is too complex and likely not quite universal.

Here is what I'd say so far:
- The approach `<CR><C-o>O` will most likely stay.
- This does look like probably some `svelte` related upstream issue.
- I am not sure what to recommend currently beside some custom 'mini.pairs' like mapping that is local only to `svelte` buffers. If `<CR><Esc>==O` works as expected (which I am in no position to verify, I am afraid), then we can help with making it a more permanent part of the config (if needed).

> This does look like probably some svelte related upstream issue.

According to @mig-hub, for filetype [astro](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2591#issuecomment-6527825408) it works.
In the neovim source, there exists a [runtime/indent/astro.vim](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/indent/astro.vim) file. There is no related svelte.vim. If I copy astro.vim to `runtime/indent/svelte.vim` verbatim and rebuild, the issue seems to be resolved.

Fun fact: That file is based on [vim-svelte](https://github.com/evanleck/vim-svelte).

@mig-hub, could you add [runtime/indent/astro.vim](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/indent/astro.vim) to your config, in the 'indent' directory? For example, to `~/.config/nvim/indent/svelte.vim`. In my repro folder, doing so solves the issue. I replaced 3 occurrences of the word 'GetAstroIndent' with 'GetSvelteIndent'...

> > This does look like probably some svelte related upstream issue.    
> According to [@mig-hub](https://github.com/mig-hub), for filetype [astro](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2591#issuecomment-6527825408) it works.
> In the neovim source, there exists a [runtime/indent/astro.vim](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/indent/astro.vim) file. There is no related svelte.vim. If I copy astro.vim to `runtime/indent/svelte.vim` verbatim and rebuild, the issue seems to be resolved.

Oh, that's nice! I forgot that this is controlled by the 'indent/' runtime directory and not 'ftplugin/' (which I looked at and didn't find anything relevant).

> [@mig-hub](https://github.com/mig-hub), could you add [runtime/indent/astro.vim](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/indent/astro.vim) to your config, in the 'indent' directory? For example, to `~/.config/nvim/indent/svelte.vim`. In my repro folder, doing so solves the issue. I replaced 3 occurrences of the word 'GetAstroIndent' with 'GetSvelteIndent'...

The easier (maybe temporary) solution is to add `~/.config/nvim/indent/svelte.vim` with a single `runtime! indent/astro.vim` line. This seems to indeed fix the issue for the repro case. I'll wait for the confirmation to be sure.

@abeldekat ,

> According to @mig-hub, for filetype https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2591#issuecomment-6527825408 it works.
> In the neovim source, there exists a [runtime/indent/astro.vim](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/indent/astro.vim) file. There is no related svelte.vim. If I copy astro.vim to runtime/indent/svelte.vim verbatim and rebuild, the issue seems to be resolved.
> 
> Fun fact: That file is based on [vim-svelte](https://github.com/evanleck/vim-svelte).

I would not be surprised because I have used `vim-polyglot` in the past. The svelte plugin used was `vim-svelte-plugin`. It has a [similar set of files in indent directory](https://github.com/leafOfTree/vim-svelte-plugin/tree/master/indent), and I did not create issues.

@echasnovski , I can confirm that if I copy the `indent/astro.vim` file in my config, rename the references to "Astro", then it works fine. The indentation is fixed.

So if I understand well, these indent files ship with `neovim` itself.

There are a few quirks like now with this file, like after a closing script tag, `o` or `<CR>` in insert mode puts my cursor on an indented line.

```svelte
<script>
  // My JS code
</script>
  |
```

It does it only after script `tags`, and it does it after `script` tags anywhere.

Definitely less of a problem. But I assume it is a conversation for Neovim repo. I don't want to pollute the Mini threads.

I will live with it for a while so that I can note all quirks and report them.

Thanks to both of you!

> [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski) , I can confirm that if I copy the `indent/astro.vim` file in my config, rename the references to "Astro", then it works fine. The indentation is fixed.

Great. Then I indeed don't think that this is a 'mini.pairs' issue.

> So if I understand well, these indent files ship with `neovim` itself.

I'd say that this is even a `vim/vim` issue. These type of runtime files Neovim (mostly) uses verbatim from Vim.

To be more argumentative, bring this up upstream without 'mini.pairs' and only with built-in capabilities used. It is reproducible with `nvim --clean` and `:set autoindent smartindent`: after pressing Insert mode `<CR>` inside `{}` it seems to produce the differently indented `}` on the new line; while later `<C-o>O` also results in more indented than expected.

title: [mini.pairs] adds extra indentation inside svelte files JS and SCSS parts
